title: What happens when we multiply by ten, a hundred, a thousand?
description: Five decimals are each multiplied by ten, one hundred and one thousand to complete a table. The first is worked with fractions, and the digits after the point are counted to decide how far the point moves, the same way as the example in the book.
teaching_notes: One idea: multiplying by ten, one hundred or one thousand moves the point one, two or three places right, and zeros are added when the point runs past the last digit. Watch for students who move the point left or forget the zeros.

source: Multiply the following numbers by 10, 100 and 1000 to complete the table: 5.7, 23.02, 0.92, 0.306, 24.67
video_script.why: The child has seen how fractions and the digits after the point work in a product and now multiplies by ten, one hundred and one thousand.
video_script.substitution: the book's table of five numbers multiplied by ten, one hundred and one thousand
video_script.anchor: A table of five decimals to be multiplied by ten, one hundred and one thousand

final_answer.spoken: the table filled for all five numbers

maths_rules: × 10 moves the point 1 place right, × 100 moves it 2 places, × 1000 moves it 3 places; zeros are added when the point runs past the last digit
size check: 24.67 is near 25, so near 250, 2500 and 25000
video_script.design: One idea: each zero in the multiplier moves the point one place right. Assumes the writing of a decimal as a fraction. The table stays all video; the first row is shown in the working and the other rows appear only on the answer beat.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>This is a question from your book.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>A table has five decimal numbers in its rows.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each number is multiplied by ten, by one hundred and by one thousand.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>What goes in the empty boxes of the table?

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>In a number, each place is ten times the place to its right.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Multiplying by ten moves every digit one place to the left.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>That is the same as moving the point one place to the right.

marks.m2: the last two numbers are written

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Given, five point seven, twenty three point zero two, and zero point nine two.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>And zero point three zero six, and twenty four point six seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Each is multiplied by ten, one hundred and one thousand.

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>We have to find all fifteen products for the table.

beats.colours: the top in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step one, solve the same way as the example in your book. Write five point seven as fifty seven over ten.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Times ten, the ten cancels, and we get fifty seven.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Times one hundred is five hundred and seventy, and times one thousand is five thousand seven hundred.

beats.colours: the digits after the point in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step two, count the digits after the point in each number.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five point seven has one, and twenty three point zero two has two.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Zero point nine two has two, and zero point three zero six has three.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Twenty four point six seven has two.

beats.on_screen: × 10 moves the point 1 place right; × 100, 2 places; × 1000, 3 places; if the point runs past the last digit, add zeros

beats.colours: the moving point in the accent colour
narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step three, times ten moves the point one place right.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Times one hundred moves it two places, and times one thousand, three places.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>If the point runs past the last digit, add zeros at the end.

beats.on_screen: Check: 24.67 is near 25, so the products are near 250, 2500 and 25000

marks.m1: twenty four point six seven is rounded to twenty five
marks.m2: twenty five is multiplied by ten and by one hundred

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>Step four, check the size. Twenty four point six seven is near twenty five.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Twenty five times ten is two hundred and fifty. Times one hundred, it is two thousand five hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Times one thousand, it is twenty five thousand. The products must be near these.

marks.m2: the first row of the table is filled
marks.m7: the rest of the fifth row is filled

narration: <bookmark mark='m1'/>The table is now complete.
<bookmark mark='m2'/>Five point seven gives fifty seven, five hundred and seventy, and five thousand seven hundred.
<bookmark mark='m3'/>Twenty three point zero two gives two hundred and thirty point two. Then two thousand three hundred and two. Then twenty three thousand and twenty.
<bookmark mark='m4'/>Zero point nine two gives nine point two, ninety two, and nine hundred and twenty.
<bookmark mark='m5'/>Zero point three zero six gives three point zero six, thirty point six, and three hundred and six.
<bookmark mark='m6'/>Twenty four point six seven gives two hundred and forty six point seven.
<bookmark mark='m7'/>Next, two thousand four hundred and sixty seven, and twenty four thousand six hundred and seventy.
